items.claim: Keep ISR query overrides out of the ordinary render handler. The ordinary `_render` handler receives `/api/public?x_astro_path=/api/private` with `x-vercel-isr: 1` and no middleware secret.
items.consequence: The built handler executes `/api/private`, including with ISR disabled, regressing the 10.0.2 path-override protection. Deployed external reach depends on Vercel header sanitization.
items.proposed_fix: Bind ISR query rewriting to an ISR-specific generated handler or authenticated metadata, and retain the secret gate on ordinary `_render` requests.

items.claim: Does Vercel prevent client-supplied ISR headers from reaching ordinary functions?
items.consequence: This determines whether the confirmed handler path-override regression is externally reachable through Vercel and changes its deployed security impact.
items.proposed_fix: Vercel platform owners can supply an authoritative header-overwrite guarantee or an end-to-end measurement sending x-vercel-isr: 1 to an ordinary route. That evidence settles the deployed reach of vercel/unauthenticated-render-path-override.
